title: Make the transfer dashboard's figures true

blocks.text: The file-transfer dashboard shows two figures: the total bytes moved today and the mean duration of the most recent transfers. On the day the team mirrored three large disk images, the total went negative. On a quiet night with no transfers at all, the dashboard said the recent transfers took 0.0 ms on average, which paged nobody but convinced someone the service was fast.

items: `totalBytes(sizes)`: the total of all the sizes;
`meanOfLast(durationsMs, n)`: the mean of the last `n` durations (all of them if there are fewer), and nothing when there are none, so the dashboard can show `n/a`.

blocks.text: The sizes and durations arrive as `int[]`. About four lines in total.

cases.says: the total is the sum of the transfer sizes, and 0 for no transfers
the recent mean averages the last n durations, or all of them when there are fewer
a total above Integer.MAX_VALUE comes out exact, not wrapped
with no durations the mean is absent, not zero, and the dashboard shows n/a
the window of recent durations includes the newest one

origin.section: Only Primitive Streams Have sum() and average(), and IntStream.sum() Overflows

concepts: IntStream.sum() returns an int and wraps silently; asLongStream().sum() or summaryStatistics().getSum() gives a long.
sum(), average() and summaryStatistics() exist only on primitive streams; average() is an OptionalDouble, empty for no elements.
